extracted.intended_audience: State Departments of Transportation (State DOTs), Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs), transportation planners, and stakeholders/commenters on the FHWA GHG performance measure rule
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for how State DOTs and MPOs must calculate, report, and set targets for a GHG performance measure (percent change in tailpipe CO2 on the NHS), plus the topics FHWA solicited comment on in the NPRM and FHWA's responses to public comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biennial reporting timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Biennial reporting related to the GHG measure is required to begin with the 2026 Full Performance Period Progress Report; State DOT 2- and 4-year targets will be reported in the 2026 Baseline Performance Period Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions to 23 CFR 490.107(b)(1)-(3) implement this timing. See discussion under 'State DOT Data for the GHG Metric Calculation' for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG metric and measure definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOTs are required to calculate and report both the GHG measure and the GHG metric. The GHG metric is defined as the calculation of tailpipe CO2 emissions on the NHS for a given year computed in million metric tons (mmt) and rounded to the nearest hundredth (23 CFR 490.511(c)). The measure is the percent change between the current year and the reference year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State DOTs use the metric to calculate the measure; metric definition and rounding conventions are specified in 23 CFR 490.511(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data inputs and source specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The data inputs State DOTs must use to calculate the metric are defined in 23 CFR 490.511(c) and the data requirements are defined in 23 CFR 490.509; FHWA will define specific data sources it will use when it calculates the metric and measure for the significant progress determination (23 CFR 490.109(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ensure consistent calculation FHWA prescribes the required data inputs and will use defined data sources for its determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of best available VMT data
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOTs may use their best available vehicle miles traveled (VMT) data when establishing targets, reporting baseline and actual performance, and discussing progress; the VMT data used should represent the prior calendar year and be consistent with the final VMT data submitted to HPMS to the maximum extent practicable (23 CFR 490.509(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change addresses that HPMS VMT may not be finalized by August 15; HPMS data as of November 30, 2023 will be used to calculate the metric for the reference year.

rubrics_metrics.name: State reporting of metric calculation components
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOTs must report the GHG metric value they calculated, the individual values used to calculate the GHG metric, and a description of the data source(s) used for the VMT information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule revisions removed the proposed requirement to report CO2 emissions on all public roads because the values used to calculate the GHG metric can be used to calculate the all-roads value. Corresponding changes were made to 23 CFR 490.511(f)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: HPMS extraction date for significant progress determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The significant progress determination will calculate the GHG metric and measure for the baseline and actual performance using the HPMS data available on November 30th of the year the significant progress determination is made; for the reference year FHWA will use HPMS data as of November 30, 2023 (23 CFR 490.109(d)(1)(vi)-(vii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fixes a consistent extraction date for FHWA's determinations and aligns reporting/calc expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: CO2 emission factors for determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The significant progress determination will use the CO2 factors specified in section 490.509(f) (see addition of 23 CFR 490.109(d)(1)(viii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA specifies which CO2 factors will be applied to ensure consistent calculations across States.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Initial GHG Report data requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: State DOTs are required to submit the State Initial GHG Report using the data specified in 23 CFR 490.107(d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA added the requirement for this report in the final rule; the report must use the specified data elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: State DOT calculation method uniformity
rubrics_metrics.description: The State DOT's method for calculating the GHG metric is defined in 23 CFR 490.511(c) and the method will be the same for all States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a uniform State-level approach to metric calculation across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPO flexibility in metric calculation and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: MPOs are granted flexibility in how they calculate the GHG metric (23 CFR 490.511(d)); MPOs must report a description of their metric calculation method(s), and when that method is not one of the ones specified in 490.511(d), the MPO must include information demonstrating the method(s) has valid and useful results for measuring transportation-related CO2 (23 CFR 490.107(c)(2)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPOs are encouraged to coordinate with State DOTs on the data used to the maximum extent practicable. The final rule removed the proposed requirement for MPOs and State DOTs to mutually agree upon a method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of part 490 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: A severability clause (23 CFR 490.515) states the amendments to part 490, including establishment and calculation of the GHG performance measure and declining targets, are capable of operating independently of one another; if one or more aspects are invalid, the remaining provisions should remain in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects the remainder of the rule if portions are struck down.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for retaining percent-change tailpipe CO2 measure
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA retained the GHG performance measure as the percent change in tailpipe CO2 emissions on the NHS compared to the reference year because of its simplicity, ease of calculation, and reliance on data States already report to FHWA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA acknowledges lifecycle emissions and other complexities but determined including them would complicate and possibly reduce reliability of the measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of lifecycle processes from the GHG measure
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA decided not to include lifecycle processes (e.g., electricity used by EVs, embodied carbon in vehicle manufacture, infrastructure construction) in the GHG measure because addressing these factors would lead to more complicated and potentially less reliable calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA noted lifecycle components are relevant but omitted them to preserve simplicity and data reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of per-capita and VMT-only measures
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA rejected commenters' suggestions to use a per-capita measure or a VMT-only measure, stating per-capita would not track total atmospheric CO2 and VMT-alone would be an indirect proxy that fails to account for benefits of highway operations, pavement strategies, electrification, and vehicle efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA favors a total tailpipe CO2 metric to track absolute emissions and progress toward emission reduction goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of State-reported fuel sales to capture fleet/speed/pavement effects
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA believes the measure sufficiently accounts for factors like roadway speed, changes in vehicle fleet efficiency, and the effect of pavement condition on fuel efficiency because these are represented through State-reported fuel sales used to calculate the measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is FHWA's technical justification for not separately adjusting the metric for those factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: FHWA not mandating specific targets or project selections
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA clarifies it is not regulating GHG emissions, not mandating any reductions, not forcing States to select specific projects, and not setting targets for States or MPOs; FHWA requires State DOTs and MPOs to set targets consistent with TPM but does not approve or disapprove individual targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The measure provides information to support decisionmaking; FHWA will not direct project selection or require achievement of particular target values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment topics solicited in the NPRM
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA requested comment on structuring improving targets and associated reporting and significant progress requirements; implementing the GHG measure within TPM to support emissions reductions; changes to the measure or implementation to improve impact; handling of joint UZA targets among MPOs; RIA assumptions about applicability, level of effort, frequency of activities and resulting burden; staff time impacts; potential economies of scale or efficiencies; and qualitative benefits or costs of implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA considered comments on these topics in developing the final rule and specifically responds to significant adverse comments in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of rural/state variation concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA considered commenters' concerns that the measure may be inappropriate for rural States or those with growing populations and that exogenous factors (population growth, goods movement, policy, etc.) affect emissions, but FHWA rejects that the measure places an unequal burden and retains the chosen metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA emphasizes the rule does not mandate reductions and that States will set targets appropriate to their conditions; FHWA also noted States and MPOs may use additional local measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of agency capacity and funding to influence emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: FHWA notes that transportation agencies have multiple programmatic tools (transit, congestion reduction, freight initiatives, EV infrastructure, bike/ped projects, etc.) and that BIL provides significant funding (listed program totals) that can help States and MPOs achieve GHG reduction targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHWA uses this as part of its response to commenters who argued agencies lack ability to influence GHG emissions materially.
